title: Tap dancers shaping the jazz arrangements
summary: Green argues big bands could not drown out the taps because dancers had music specially orchestrated, so tap changed the jazz played.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: It's funny, now, at this time it really was beginning to be the dancers with the jazz -- dancers with jazz --
Music.
-- music.
Yes.
This is interesting.
So, now the big bands were becoming the prominent feature of the show.
Yes.
They were on the stage. And the tap dance -- what happend to tap dancing? Didn't the big bands tend to drown out the taps?

Well, they tried to, but they couldn't do this because of the tap dancers themselves -- they was always introducing these degrees, and they would always have their own music especially orchestrated to fit their tap dancing. But they would always have some kind of new jazz arrangements, because it was specially written for tap dancing. Therefore, the musicians had to play a different type of jazz.
So, basically the tap dancers were affecting the type of jazz that was being done.
Yes, but it was improving. It was all for
the best, see. They couldn't do any worse -- they had just come out of the depression.
Well, it made a large, glittery show -- big band on stage.
But how did the music -- the actual music begin to change?
Well, the music changed because of the tap dancers. They would always have their music specially written for them, you see.
No, I mean the type of music.

Well, it didn't change. It became popular. I mean, swing is what was going out and jazz was coming in, see. Jazz was beginnig to be recognized as a happier -- the happiest music they were playing, and the tap dancing going along with it made it more recognizable, see.
This was what period of time?
Well, this was in the early 40's, right after the battle of the bands.
